questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to write a good shopping list
Famous songs about shopping
Why lists are so common and why people like them
How supermarkets organise their products
questions.why: They explore our love of lists and find out why people use them so much.

questions.q: What often happens to linguistics researcher Jo Nolan in the supermarket?
options: She finds shopping lists that other people have left
She forgets to bring her shopping list
She often meets people who have read her new book about lists
She buys the wrong things by mistake
questions.why: Beth describes finding someone's shopping list and says this happens a lot to Jo.

questions.q: What was Jo really reminding herself to buy with the word 'puke'?
options: Bananas
Mushrooms
Medicine for sickness
Cucumbers
questions.why: Jo explains that her husband has always called cucumber 'puke'.

questions.q: Why does Jo's husband use the word 'puke' for this item?
options: It is the word that people use for it in his home town in Scotland
He dislikes it, and the word sounds like its short form
It was a joke from a famous song
He can't spell the real word
questions.why: He doesn't like cucumber, and 'puke' rhymes with the abbreviation 'cuc'.

questions.q: What does Phil say about lists after hearing Jo's example?
options: They are usually boring to read
They can sometimes be like secret codes
They are only useful for shopping
They should always use full words so that nobody gets confused
questions.why: Phil says, 'Sometimes lists are like secret codes.'

questions.q: What does Jo say about the list in the song My Favourite Things?
options: It is too long for people to remember
It was written to sell more records
It uses long, beautiful words to describe each favourite thing
It gives a lot in a few words and gets to the point
questions.why: She says you get 'a big bang for your buck' and 'get to the nub of things quite quickly'.

questions.q: How does Jo's friend use pros and cons lists?
options: To help her decide what to do
To plan her weekly shopping
To remember her friends' birthdays
To prepare for job interviews
questions.why: Jo says the list helps her friend resolve a situation, and by the end 'she knows what she's doing'.

questions.q: Why does Beth mention therapists near the end?
options: To warn that making too many lists causes stress
To explain that therapists write lists about patients
To show that lists can even help people feel happier
To say that therapists dislike to-do lists
questions.why: She says therapists recommend listing the good things in your life to feel happier.
